title: The Vvaan Adds Rs 2 Crore on Second Saturday as Drishyam 3 Eats Screens
excerpt: Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia's supernatural thriller slowed sharply in its second weekend against the Ajay Devgn blockbuster, but trade watchers call its Rs 55 crore run a recovery from a 'dead on arrival' forecast.
body:
• The Vvaan earned Rs 2 crore on its second Saturday, a drop of nearly 40 per cent from Friday's Rs 3.25 crore, taking its India nett total to Rs 55 crore, according to Pinkvilla's trade estimates.
  • The second weekend is expected to close at Rs 8-9 crore, lifting the total to Rs 58-59 crore — an "average" verdict, and one trade watchers say would have been a "hit" without Drishyam 3's arrival.
  • Bihar remains the film's strongest territory, powered by its Chhath Puja storyline and rural setting.
  • Run-rate math: a Rs 8-9 crore second weekend would put the India nett cume at Rs 58-59 crore, with overseas business adding roughly Rs 6 crore on top.

Second Saturday slows against Drishyam 3

The Vvaan: Force of the Forest collected Rs 2 crore on its second Saturday at the Indian box office, falling nearly 40 per cent from the Rs 3.25 crore it earned on the second Friday. The decline — sharp for a day that usually brings a weekend bump — took the Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia starrer's running total to Rs 55 crore nett, according to trade estimates compiled by Pinkvilla.

The day-wise breakdown shows a film fighting for breathing room. After a first week of Rs 49.75 crore, the second Friday held at Rs 3.25 crore, a solid result given that Ajay Devgn's Drishyam: The Conclusion released on October 2 and began pulling screens and show timings. But Saturday's slide to Rs 2 crore indicates the blockbuster's pull is now weighing on the smaller film.

Trade estimates put the second weekend's likely close at Rs 8-9 crore, which would take the entire cume to Rs 58-59 crore nett. Trade analysts quoted by Pinkvilla rate the film an AVERAGE — and add that it needed to hold better this weekend for a HIT verdict, one it likely would have earned had it not faced the Drishyam 3 storm.

From dead-on-arrival to a respectable run

The Vvaan's second-weekend fight looks different when set against where it started. Directed by Deepak Kumar Mishra, the supernatural thriller follows Rishi, an engineer who returns to his ancestral village in Bihar with his wife to settle a family property dispute. When a development project threatens a sacred forest, he is drawn into a centuries-old mystery where myth and reality collide.

The film, which also features Anup Soni, Sunil Grover, Shweta Tiwari and Maniesh Paul, is among the first Bollywood releases to build its story around Chhath Puja and the Vaan Devi folklore. A month before release, Pinkvilla reported that the film seemed "dead on arrival" — which makes a Rs 55 crore total, and counting, a genuine recovery.

Its strongest business has come from the Bihar region, where the Chhath Puja plot has given the film a distinct regional identity. That local connection has held up in smaller centres even as metro multiplexes tilt toward the newer release.

The Drishyam 3 factor

The timing of the second weekend was unforgiving. Drishyam: The Conclusion opened to outsized numbers and, as the technosports box-office tracker noted, is "taking over screens and attention" — the obvious reason a film that usually gains on Saturdays dropped instead. Screen reductions in week two have compounded the pressure.

Still, holding at Rs 3.25 crore on the second Friday, with roughly 42 per cent occupancy across about 2,144 shows according to trade tracker Khel Ja, suggests a core audience remains. The film also continues to pull modest overseas business, with trade trackers putting its international gross at roughly Rs 6 crore.

What diaspora audiences are watching

For Indians abroad, The Vvaan's run matters beyond the numbers. The film's Bihar and Jharkhand diaspora — among the largest Indian communities in the Gulf and a growing presence in the United States — get a rare mainstream portrayal of their home region's culture, built around a festival that many celebrate away from home.

Overseas collections of roughly Rs 6 crore gross show the film has found that audience, even if it has not broken out. In Gulf markets, where weekday evening shows sustain smaller Hindi releases, the second-weekend hold will decide how long exhibitors keep it on screens.

What's next

The verdict now hinges on the second-week weekdays. If the film can stabilise after the Saturday dip, Rs 58-59 crore by Sunday night leaves it within reach of the Rs 60 crore mark over the coming week — a milestone that would cement the "respectable" tag even without a hit verdict.

The question is how many screens it keeps. With Drishyam 3 dominating multiplexes and new releases queueing up through October, The Vvaan's remaining run depends on the smaller-centre and regional business that has carried it this far.
